summary: Isolate errors by targeting one device with --limit or an ad hoc eos_command run of ? with network_cli, -u and -k, combined with logging if it still fails.
questions: How do I test connectivity to one network device?
How can I narrow down a failing network playbook?

answer_card.title: Isolate a network error
answer_card.answer_md:
Target a single device:
```shell
ansible -m arista.eos.eos_command -a 'commands=?' -i inventory switch1.example.net \
  -e 'ansible_connection=ansible.netcommon.network_cli' -u admin -k
```
(`-k` not needed with working SSH keys.) Or `ansible-playbook --limit switch1.example.net`. If it still fails, set `ANSIBLE_LOG_PATH` and `ANSIBLE_DEBUG=True`, run with `-vvvv`, and check the log.
